newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid says FTC closes investigation.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid says FTC closes investigation.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp said Monday the Federal Trade Commission closed its investigation into the refusal of Rite Aid and other chain drug stores to particpate in a prescription drug plan for Maryland state employees with Merck and Co Inc's Merck Medco unit.
"The commision advises Rite Aid that its review led to conclude that it now appears that no further action is warranted by the commission," a Rite Aid statement said.

Rite Aid's chief executive Martin Grass said in the statement the commission's action "strengthens our resolve to defend the unfounded civil action that Merck Medco is pursuing against us in this matter."
"If our analysis of a prescription drug plan leads us to conclude that we are not offered a fair price, then we will not participate," Grass added.
A Merck spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
Rite Aid said December 20, 1995 it would no longer fill prescriptions of the Maryland plan starting January 1, 1996.
